title: Termination of the Designation of South Sudan for Temporary Protected Status
summary:
The United States will end Temporary Protected Status for South Sudan on January 5, 2026. Homeland Security says conditions have improved enough to allow return, and that continuing the program is not in the national interest.

Officials point to a reduced risk of large-scale conflict, efforts by the United Nations to strengthen local policing and justice, and ongoing projects that are improving infrastructure and local governance. They also note that South Sudan’s government is accepting the return of its citizens and that many people have already gone back since a 2018 peace deal. The decision also reflects a broader policy push to keep temporary programs tightly aligned with what the law requires. Homeland Security cited foreign policy goals, immigration enforcement priorities, and some public safety and fraud concerns within a portion of the group as part of its rationale. As of early October, about 232 people currently held this status, with 73 applications pending.

Who might see this as a positive step? United States agencies focused on immigration enforcement and foreign policy say it sends a consistent message and supports cooperation with South Sudan on returns. Some will argue it reflects improved conditions on the ground and a move toward normalizing travel and migration between the two countries.

Who is likely to feel the impact most? South Sudanese nationals and their families who have relied on this protection, as well as their employers and communities in the United States. Work permits tied to this status remain valid through January 5, 2026, and there is a 60‑day transition window, but after that date people without another valid status will lose protection from removal. Supporters of the program may worry that conditions in South Sudan remain fragile and that ending it now could put some people at risk or disrupt workplaces and communities. Anyone affected should review their options and, if possible, seek qualified legal guidance.

Also noted in the same Federal Register issue: the Postal Service filed to add a new international shipping agreement, and the United States Mint announced a public meeting of the Citizens Coinage Advisory Committee on November 18, 2025.
